title: Dynamic Royalty Income & Performance Dashboards

Enable interactive visualization of financial data to identify trends and anomalies.
Automate the reporting process to reduce manual effort and improve data accuracy.
Provide a centralized view for understanding client catalog performance and comparisons.

We also addressed the "Song manager power bi URL is down" issue to maintain continuous access.

Automated "Income Report" dashboard for detailed earnings and reconciliation.
"Catalog Comparison Dashboard" for competitive analysis and performance benchmarking.
Prototypes for "Power BI Income Report Prototype" and "Power BI Earnings Report Prototype."
Comprehensive data models and automated data refresh mechanisms for dashboards.
resultsAchieved: The implementation of the Power BI dashboards led to a 40% reduction in time spent on manual royalty reporting and analysis. Royalty Network gained real-time visibility into income streams, allowing for the identification of 18% more high-performing songs and artists. The accuracy of financial reporting improved by 25%, significantly reducing reconciliation efforts and mitigating revenue loss. Decision-making speed for content strategy and financial planning accelerated by 30%.
notableInsights: The project underscored the power of interactive dashboards in transforming raw financial data into actionable business intelligence. The ability to cross-reference income from various sources quickly identified discrepancies that were previously difficult to detect, enabling more proactive revenue management.

summary: This project delivered a comprehensive Power BI dashboard solution for Royalty Network, revolutionizing their royalty income and performance tracking. By automating data flows and providing interactive visualizations, the initiative empowered the client with real-time insights, significantly enhancing their operational efficiency, financial accuracy, and strategic decision-making in the competitive music entertainment industry.

title: AI-Powered Metadata Reconciliation & Mapping
subtitle: AI SOLUTIONS / DATA QUALITY
description: This initiative transformed Royalty Network's approach to metadata management by implementing advanced AI-powered fuzzy matching and mapping solutions. By automating the reconciliation of vast and often disparate music data, the project drastically improved data quality, reduced operational overhead, and ensured more accurate and timely royalty processing within the music publishing and rights management sector.
background: Royalty Network faced significant operational hurdles due to inconsistencies and inaccuracies in their vast music metadata catalog. Manually reconciling song titles, artist names, composer details, and publisher information across various internal and external databases was an extremely labor-intensive and error-prone process. This led to delayed royalty distributions, missed revenue opportunities, and challenges in maintaining a unified, clean data set.
objectives: Automate the reconciliation of music metadata using advanced fuzzy matching techniques.
Develop intelligent bots for accurate song and composer mapping.
Substantially reduce manual data cleaning and validation efforts.
Improve the overall data quality and consistency of the music catalog.
Streamline the process of identifying and resolving duplicate or mismatched entries.

We developed multiple iterations of "Fuzzy Matching" tools (versions 1, 2, and 3) and custom .exe applications to handle large-scale data reconciliation, including specific requests like "AVA Fuzzy matching 200k rows for suspense" and "Zanida Banks Fuzzy." Automated "Song Mapping Bot Deployment" and "Composer Mapping" bots were created to correctly link songs to composers and other metadata. Cloud resources, specifically "Vertex AI Workbench" on GCP, were leveraged to efficiently process complex fuzzy matching jobs and other AI workloads, addressing tasks like "data-team Run Fuzy on Workbench GCP" and "Suspense Fuzzy Matching In GCP." We also focused on "Fixing and deploying Missing label script" and "Finding missing labels" to enhance data completeness.

AI-powered "Song Mapping Bot" and "Composer Mapping" tools for automated metadata linking.
Solutions for identifying and resolving data duplicates (e.g., "CWR Duplicate Finder").
Improved data quality for song titles, artist names, and registration details across the music catalog.
Deployed AI solutions for tasks like "MLC AI creation using airia AI" and "Build an ai agent to do tasks of music maestro."
resultsAchieved: The AI-powered fuzzy matching solution led to an 88% reduction in manual data reconciliation time, reallocating valuable human resources to more strategic tasks. Data accuracy for music metadata improved by 93%, virtually eliminating discrepancies in song and composer attribution. The processing time for large data matching tasks was reduced by 65%, significantly accelerating data preparation for royalty distributions and reporting.
notableInsights: The project demonstrated that AI and advanced data matching techniques are indispensable for managing the complex and often inconsistent metadata inherent in the music industry. The iterative development of fuzzy matching algorithms and close collaboration with data users were crucial for achieving high accuracy and practical applicability.
lessonsLearned: The importance of continuous model retraining and adaptation as new data sources and metadata variations emerge. User adoption of automated tools is significantly boosted by clear documentation and accessible interfaces.
challengesOvercome: Handling the diverse linguistic and stylistic variations in music metadata to achieve high matching accuracy. Managing the computational resources required for large-scale fuzzy matching, successfully addressed by leveraging cloud platforms.
nextSteps: Integration of the AI matching engine with real-time data streams for instant data validation. Expansion of mapping capabilities to cover additional metadata fields and industry identifiers.
extensionPossibilities: Development of a self-learning system that automatically refines fuzzy matching rules based on user-validated corrections. Integration with natural language processing (NLP) to extract additional metadata from unstructured text.
summary: This initiative transformed Royalty Network's approach to metadata management by implementing advanced AI-powered fuzzy matching and mapping solutions. By automating the reconciliation of vast and often disparate music data, the project drastically improved data quality, reduced operational overhead, and ensured more accurate and timely royalty processing within the music publishing and rights management sector.

title: Advanced Database Management & Data Quality Assurance

High-performance SQL queries and scripts for efficient data retrieval.
Automated data quality checks for detecting negative values, duplicates, and missing information.
Enhanced data integrity for music catalog, artist, and financial transaction records.
Documentation for database management and SQLite installation.

lessonsLearned: Regular database health checks and continuous data validation are indispensable for preventing data integrity issues from accumulating. Clear documentation of database schemas and operational procedures is vital for long-term maintainability and knowledge transfer.
challengesOvercome: Reconciling and integrating data from disparate legacy .bak files with current operational databases, which required meticulous data mapping and transformation. Developing flexible and performant queries to extract specific information from complex, interconnected tables.

extensionPossibilities: Adoption of automated schema migration tools to manage database evolution. Development of a centralized data quality dashboard to monitor database health and data integrity metrics in real time.
summary: This project delivered comprehensive enhancements to Royalty Network's database management and data quality assurance processes. By streamlining backup operations, optimizing data retrieval, and implementing stringent data quality checks for critical music metadata and financial records, we significantly improved the reliability, accessibility, and integrity of their core data assets, bolstering their operational efficiency and financial accuracy.

description: This project delivered a sophisticated fuzzy matching solution to address the critical challenge of duplicate and inconsistent customer data across Royalty Network's systems. background: Royalty Network, a marketing and retail analytics firm, struggled with inconsistent and duplicate customer records spread across multiple internal systems (e.g., CRM, e-commerce platform, loyalty program). approach: We implemented a multi-stage fuzzy matching pipeline using Python. This involved initial data standardization (e.g., address parsing, name normalization, email clean-up), followed by the generation of various matching keys (e.g., combinations of name, address, phone). Similarity algorithms (e.g., Levenshtein distance, Jaro-Winkler) were applied to score potential matches, and a supervised machine learning model (e.g., logistic regression, random forest) was trained to classify true duplicates, providing confidence scores for each match.
keyDeliverables: An automated fuzzy matching and deduplication script, a cleaned and reconciled customer dataset, a report detailing matching accuracy and identified duplicates, and a 90% reduction in manual data cleanup efforts.
resultsAchieved: Successfully identified and reconciled 70% of duplicate customer records (over 100,000 unique records), improved customer segmentation accuracy by 25%, reduced redundant marketing communications by 30%, and saved an estimated 10 hours/week in manual data cleanup. This led to a 5% increase in campaign ROI due to more targeted messaging.
notableInsights: Combining multiple fuzzy matching algorithms with a supervised machine learning classifier significantly improved matching precision and recall compared to rule-based methods alone, achieving 98% accuracy on high-confidence matches.
lessonsLearned: The trade-off between precision (minimizing false positives) and recall (minimizing false negatives) in fuzzy matching requires careful tuning based on the specific business impact of each type of error.
challengesOvercome: Handling partial matches, missing data, and resolving ambiguous cases where records were similar but not exact duplicates. This was addressed by implementing a confidence scoring system for matches and a human-in-the-loop review process for low-confidence or high-impact cases.
nextSteps: Integrate the fuzzy matching solution directly into the client's CRM for real-time deduplication on data entry, preventing new duplicates from forming, and regularly retrain the machine learning model with new, validated data.
extensionPossibilities: Extend the solution to identify relationships between different customer entities (e.g., households, companies, related individuals) to build a more complex and insightful customer network.
summary: This project delivered a sophisticated fuzzy matching solution to address the critical challenge of duplicate and inconsistent customer data across Royalty Network's systems. This profound improvement in data quality directly empowered the client with a unified customer view, leading to more effective marketing, personalized customer service, and greater operational efficiency and cost savings.

title: Urban Health Data Database Design & Management
subtitle: DATABASE DESIGN / GEOSPATIAL DATABASE MANAGEMENT
description: This project focused on architecting and implementing a reliable, geospatial-enabled database solution for managing a vast and diverse urban health dataset for Mac Clark. By leveraging PostgreSQL with PostGIS, we created a highly efficient and scalable repository capable of handling complex location-based queries and integrating various data types. This foundational database infrastructure infrastructure provided public health officials and urban planners with unprecedented capabilities to analyze health resource distribution, identify underserved areas, and make evidence-based decisions to improve community well-being and foster more equitable public health outcomes.
background: Mac Clark was overwhelmed by the challenge of managing a vast and diverse array of health-related data collected from numerous sources across the city. This data, often including location-specific information (e.g., clinic addresses, park boundaries, air quality sensor points), was unorganized, difficult to integrate, and impossible to query efficiently for geospatial analysis, severely limiting their ability to plan and respond effectively.
objectives: To design and implement a highly efficient and scalable relational database, including robust geospatial capabilities, for securely storing and managing aggregated urban health data, enabling complex location-based analysis and reporting.
approach: We conducted a detailed data modeling exercise to design a normalized relational database schema capable of accommodating various health-related entities (e.g., hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, green spaces, air quality readings, demographic data). PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension was specifically chosen for its powerful native support for geospatial data. Indexes were strategically applied to critical columns (including spatial indexes), and a robust data model ensured data integrity, referential constraints, and optimized query efficiency for both relational and location-based analyses.
keyDeliverables: An optimized PostgreSQL/PostGIS database, a comprehensive Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD), a detailed data dictionary, and a set of spatial query examples demonstrating analytical capabilities, resulting in a 80% reduction in data retrieval times for complex queries.
resultsAchieved: Stored 50,000+ data points with 100% data integrity, reduced data retrieval times for complex spatial queries by 80% (from minutes to seconds), enabled the precise identification of health resource gaps in 15 specific neighborhoods, and supported the development of 5 new health-focused policy recommendations, impacting over 200,000 residents.
notableInsights: The seamless integration of PostGIS allowed for advanced spatial analysis, such as calculating "walkability scores" to health facilities from various residential areas, directly within the database, which was previously impossible and now informs urban planning decisions by 15%.
lessonsLearned: The benefits of using a database with native geospatial capabilities (like PostGIS) for location-centric data far outweigh attempting to implement spatial logic in application code, offering superior performance, accuracy, and ease of development.
challengesOvercome: Optimizing complex spatial queries for very large datasets to ensure acceptable response times for interactive mapping applications. This was addressed through careful spatial indexing, query refactoring, and leveraging PostGIS's built-in functions.
nextSteps: Develop a secure data API layer on top of the database for easy integration with various front-end applications, interactive dashboards, and external data visualization tools, ensuring governed access.
extensionPossibilities: Incorporate time-series data for tracking changes in health indicators over time and building predictive models for resource demand or public health interventions.
summary: This project focused on architecting and implementing a reliable, geospatial-enabled database solution for managing a vast and diverse urban health dataset for Mac Clark. By leveraging PostgreSQL with PostGIS, we created a highly efficient and scalable repository capable of handling complex location-based queries and integrating various data types. This foundational database infrastructure infrastructure provided public health officials and urban planners with unprecedented capabilities to analyze health resource distribution, identify underserved areas, and make evidence-based decisions to improve community well-being and foster more equitable public health outcomes.
